title: Hotel check-in
setting: A business hotel in Osaka, 3pm. You have a booking under your name.

n1.speaker: staff
n1.japanese: いらっしゃいませ。ご予約のお客様でしょうか。
n1.romaji: Irasshaimase. Go-yoyaku no o-kyakusama deshō ka.
n1.english: Welcome. Do you have a reservation?
n1.audioHint: いらっしゃいませ。ごよやくのおきゃくさまでしょうか

options.feedback: Yes. Follow with your name and hand over your passport — they're required to copy it for foreign guests.
Slightly ahead of the question, but it answers it implicitly and moves things along.
The honorific padding (ご〜, お客様, でしょうか) makes hotel Japanese sound much longer than it is. The core is just 予約 — reservation.

n2.speaker: staff
n2.audioHint: おなまえをうかがえますか

options.feedback: Surname + です is all that's needed. Showing the booking confirmation alongside removes any spelling problem.

options.japanese: これが予約のメールです。
options.romaji: Kore ga yoyaku no mēru desu.
options.feedback: Efficient. 伺えます is humble-form 'ask' — you'll meet a lot of this register in hotels.

n3.speaker: staff
n3.japanese: ありがとうございます。三泊でお間違いないでしょうか。

furigana.b: ありがとうございます。

n3.romaji: Arigatō gozaimasu. Sanpaku de o-machigai nai deshō ka.
n3.english: Thank you. Three nights — is that correct?
n3.audioHint: ありがとうございます。さんぱくでおまちがいないでしょうか

options.feedback: そうです confirms a statement. Note 三泊 is さんぱく — the counter for nights shifts sound at 1, 3, 6, 8 and 10.
Good moment to ask if you want to extend — much easier now than on your last morning.
Understood, but a bare はい to a confirmation question is thin. はい、そうです is barely longer and much clearer.

n4.speaker: staff
n4.japanese: お部屋は八階です。朝食は六時半からとなっております。

furigana.b: からとなっております。

n4.romaji: O-heya wa hachikai desu. Chōshoku wa rokuji han kara to natte orimasu.
n4.english: Your room is on the 8th floor. Breakfast is from 6:30.
n4.audioHint: おへやははちかいです。ちょうしょくはろくじはんからとなっております

options.feedback: Ask now — the password is usually on a card they'll hand you with the key.
Worth confirming. Business hotels are typically 10am, earlier than most travellers assume.
Fine. 半 = half past, and となっております is just an ornate 'is' — the content is 六時半から.

n5.speaker: staff
n5.japanese: こちらが鍵になります。ごゆっくりどうぞ。

furigana.b: になります。ごゆっくりどうぞ。

n5.romaji: Kochira ga kagi ni narimasu. Go-yukkuri dōzo.
n5.english: Here is your key. Please enjoy your stay.
n5.audioHint: こちらがかぎになります。ごゆっくりどうぞ

options.feedback: Done. ごゆっくり means 'take your time / relax' — a warm close, not an instruction.
If you're heading out before the room is ready, this is the moment. Nearly every hotel will hold bags.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Checked in. Hotel staff use heavy honorific register — long sentences, small content. Listen for the nouns: 予約, 名前, 泊, 階, 朝食, 鍵.
